main_text.p: {*}τούτοις διεξιών, αὐτὰ αἱ γυναῖκες ἐκ τῆς ὁδῷ τὰς παριόντας ἁρπάζεσι· ἢ κακῶς λεγόντων ἑτέρων σω-ἐπιλαμβάνεσθαι ἢ αὐ-{*}τὸς, λέγων, ἢ ἐγὼ Τε-τὸν τὸν ἄνθρωπον πάντων μεμίσηκα, ἢ ὃ εἰδεχθής τις ὑπὸ τῷ προσώπῳ ὄψιν ἢ δὲ πονηρία ὑδὲν ὁ-μοιον. σημεῖον ᾧ, τῇ ἢ ἑαυτῆ γυναικὶ τρεῖς χαλκὰς εἰς ὀ-λον δίδωσι. καὶ τὰ ψυχρὰ λέγεσθαι[?] ἀναγ-κάζει τὸ Ποσειδῶνος {*}ἡμέρα. ἡ συγκαθή-μενος δεινὸς ᾧσεὶ {*}τὸ ἀνασάντος εἰπεῖν. ἢ ἄλλα πλεῖστα ᾧσεὶ τῶν φίλων ἢ οἰκείων τελευτηκότων κακῶς

Τέλος de absente detrahentibus, idem facit ipse quoque, & ait, Ego etiam hunc hominem omnium odi maxime. Etenim si faciem spectes, turpis est & quem merito oderis: si impro-bitatem, nihil ei simile. Scias ita esse, cum uxori tres aeris nummulos in opsonium dare soleat: & ut Posidone mèse frigi-da lauet, cogere. Moris etiam habet, sedens inter plures, furgere ut aliquē accuset: plurimáque alia de amicis & familiaribus suis male loqui:& de ipsis etiam mortuis detrahere.
καὶ εἰπεῖν, ἢ ὡς εἰ τῶν π-[?]

page.notes: Asterisk reference marks stand in the left margin beside lines 1, 7, 19 and 21; the margin notes they point to are not visible on this part and are not transcribed. A stray mark in the left margin around the middle of the page is not printed text and is left out. Some Greek letters and accents are uncertain, especially in the lines marked [?] and where the text runs to the cut edge. The first word of the page is a fragment and carries a printed italic word "abente", read as "absente". The Greek lines are partly cut at the left edge and their readings are doubtful, so they are marked [?]. The running head's first letter is doubtful. The text "Posidone" and "mèse" are copied as printed and may be misprinted.
